CXII. In nomine domini amen. Qnia omnes morimur et quasi aque, que non reuertuntur, dilabuntur, et qui semel exit, non reuertitur ad penitenciam peragendam, eapropter decet quemlibet Christianum considerare nouissima sua, ut ueniente sponso cum prudentibus me- reatur ingredi uirginibus ad nupcias leticie sempiterno. Ego igitur Vlricus dictus de Drochaw sano consilio oonsensu et vnanimi uolun- tate heredum meorum, quippe cum bona nostra mobilia et inmobilia cum dictis beredibus mois adhuc babeantur communiter indiuisa, assistent« eciam ad hoc deliberacione ac uoluntate nobilium uirorum et dominorum meorum videlicet domini Petri domini Jodoci domini VIrici domini Johannis dictorum de Rosenherch nee non omnium ami- corum meorum, qui huiusmodi libenter et fauorabiliter admiserunt, ut deusuenie largitor et humane salutis auctor michi det in hoc mundo sie uiuere, ut transcursus huius mundi tenebris, ubi nichil certum habe- mus, dignetur perducere ad futuram, quam inquirimus ciuitatem. Do presentibus lego statuo testor et assigno ecclesie parochiali sancti Nycolay in Rosenberch et plebano pro tempore existenti perpetuis temporibus duraturum (sic) pratum adiacens Multauie sub uilla dicta Korith pro animabus videlicet Hermanni bone memorie quondam nati Przybysslay pie recordacionis, qui quondam tenuerunt residenciam corporalem in castro Rosenberch, mea omnium predecessorum suo- cessorumque meorum sic, quod exnunc me uiuente et post mortem meam perpetuis temporibus percipiat omni anno dictus plebanus prouentus dicti prati et ecclesia supradicta. Et quia nobilis animus nouit refundere beneficium, quod accepit, ipse plebanus ecclesie prius dicte videlicet in Rosenberch se michi firmius astrinxit promit- lens nomine suo et suorum omnium suoccessorum plebanorum seu legittimorum rectorum superius dicte ecclesie, quod singulis annis in die sancti Galli ipse plebanus cantabit et omnes successores sui uigilias defunctorum cum nouem lectionibus, datis etiam quatuor can- delis ad dictas vigilias ardentibus, et in crastino sex missas defunc torum tenebit, uocatis sacerdotibus et rogatis, qui dictas missas fuerint celebraturi, qui quidem sacerdotes dictas missas officiantes 124 Hermanni mee progenitorum successorum meorum et omnium fide- liuiii defunctorum habentes memoriam animarum deo patri hostiam offerant salutarem. Quos quidem etiam sacerdotes iam numeratos uocatis etiam decem pauperibus promittit pascere supradictus pleba- nus ac reficere in prandio laute et honeste. Verum si iam dictus plebanus predicti promissi aliquid infringeret ita, quod die prefixa dictum seruicium uel sequenti tercia quarta quinta sexta septima et maxime octaua die cum refectione prius dictorum sacerdotum et pauperum facere negligenter obmitteret, extunc evolso vno mense amota omni crastinacione obligauit se et successores suos plebanos ad penam sexaginta denariorum Wyennensium pro dicta ecclesia daturum. Sin autem hoc idem pluribus mensibus facere neglexeril, prius dicte pene promittit se et succe ssores suos subiacere tam diu, quousque singula predicta ipse et sequaces sui cum effectu fuerint exsecuti. Vitricus autem ecclesie eiusdem in Rosenberch plenum posse monendi cum ceteris ciuibus de pena obligata habebit. Et ut testamento ordinationi legacioni et statuto predictis nullus aliquando ualeat contraire sigillum meum vna cum sigillis dominorum videlicet nobilis viri domini Petri de Rosenberch domini Marquardy de Pores- syn Marquardi de Metlyn et VIrici filii mei presentibus est appen- sum. entries.english:
1361, undated. Ulrich called von Drochaw gives as freehold to the parish church of Saint Nicholas at Rosenberg and its incumbent parish priest a meadow lying on the Vltava below the village of Nirschlern.

CXII. In the name of the Lord, amen. Since we all die and pass away like waters that do not return, and whoever has departed does not return to do penance, it is fitting for every Christian to consider his last things, so that when the bridegroom comes he may merit, with the prudent virgins, to enter the wedding feast of everlasting joy. Therefore I, Ulrich called von Drochaw, with the sound counsel, consent, and unanimous will of my heirs—for our movable and immovable property is still held jointly and undivided with those heirs—and also with the deliberation and will of my noble lords, Lord Peter, Lord Jodok, Lord Ulrich, and Lord Johann von Rosenberg, and of all my friends, who have willingly and favorably accepted this, give, bequeath, establish, attest, and assign to the parish church of Saint Nicholas at Rosenberg and its incumbent parish priest, in perpetuity, the meadow beside the Vltava below the village called Korith, for the souls of Hermann, of blessed memory, formerly son of Przybysslay, of pious remembrance, who once lived bodily in Rosenberg Castle, and of all my predecessors and successors. Thus, from now while I am alive and after my death, the said parish priest and church shall receive the meadow's income every year in perpetuity. Since a noble spirit knows how to repay a benefit received, the aforesaid parish priest at Rosenberg has bound himself firmly to me, promising in his own name and in the names of all his successors, the parish priests or lawful rectors of that church, that each year on Saint Gall's day he and his successors will sing the Office of the Dead with nine lessons, with four candles lit for the office, and on the following day will hold six masses for the dead, calling and requesting priests to celebrate those masses, who shall offer a saving sacrifice to God the Father, remembering Hermann, my forebears, my successors, and all the faithful departed. The said parish priest also promises to feed and refresh in an honorable and plentiful dinner the priests just mentioned, as well as ten poor people. If the said parish priest should fail in any part of this promise, negligently omitting to perform the service on the appointed day or on the next, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, or especially eighth day, together with the meal for the aforesaid priests and poor, then after one month, without further delay, he and his successors are bound to pay a penalty of sixty Viennese denarii to the said church. If they neglect this for several months, he and his successors promise to remain subject to the aforesaid penalty until each of these requirements has been carried out in full. The churchwarden of that church at Rosenberg shall have full power, together with the other citizens, to demand the penalty owed. And so that no one may ever contravene the aforesaid testament, ordinance, bequest, and statute, my seal, together with the seals of the lords—the noble Lord Peter von Rosenberg, Lord Marquard von Pořešín, Marquard von Metlyn, and my son Ulrich—is attached to this document. Given and done in the year of the Lord 1361. Five seals hang from parchment strips, poorly impressed; the second is in red wax, the others in white. The descriptions identify the seals and their inscriptions.
